notes: EIGHT BLOCKS, EIGHT SECTIONS ROWS, EIGHT TOC_LINKS ROWS, ONE ANCHOR APIECE. The page's
eight content bands — what, issues, process, options, why-us, cost, results, faq — are
the `sections` repeater's eight rows in the template's own order, and the eight
`toc_links` anchors are the same eight names in the same order. Verified live against
/graphql for this route. There is no code_section: this page renders no <LocalTrust> and
nothing else on it stays in code.
THE BAND COMMENTS IN THE TEMPLATE WERE WRONG AND THE STYLESHEET IS WHAT WAS READ. The
file header called #issues, #why-us and #results "cream" and #process "sage". Neither is
what the sheet paints. This page was cloned from porcelain-veneers.css INCLUDING its band
vocabulary, so `.section.alt` is CHARCOAL (smile-makeover.css:258 ->
var(--vs-charcoal-green), with h2 #fff at :262 and p rgba(255,255,255,0.85) at :264) and
`.section.dark` is SAGE-PALE (smile-makeover.css:267 -> var(--vs-sage-pale), with h2
var(--vs-ink) at :271). `cream` and `sage` are different BLOCK_BANDS choices painting
different tokens, and the page sheet defines no `.section.cream` and no `.section.sage`
rule at all — grep returns zero — so taking the comments at their word would have painted
four of these eight bands with classes this stylesheet has never styled. Each
`band_evidence` below names the rule it was read from. The template comments have been
corrected in the same commit as this file.
THE `cards` REPEATER HOLDS FIVE ROWS AND THEY ARE MOVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. Group
`issuesList`, title filled, body and meta null on all five — confirmed live. They are the
same five lines the template's `issuesList` array holds, so the `issues` block below reads
them with a `cards` row_kind. Every OTHER card, tier and paragraph in this file is a
literal, because no other group exists on this route.
THE `process_steps` REPEATER IS NULL ON THIS PAGE AND NO BLOCK ASKS FOR IT. #process is
not a numbered-steps band at all — it is the `.natural-grid` shape with a pull quote, so it
maps to media_split. That is also why nothing here uses the `columns: 5` choice the
process_steps select gained; the five-across grid on this page is #issues, and that is
card_grid, whose select still stops at 4.
ALL EIGHT ctaLabel / ctaHref PAIRS ON THE `sections` ROWS COME BACK NULL — verified live —
so there was never anything to move. Five bands ship buttons and they split four ways:
`options` and `faq` have theirs drawn by their components (ComparisonCardsBlock owns its
whole cta-row; FaqBlock owns the phone button), `what` carries a transcribed pair because
media_split gates its row on cta_label, and `process` and `results` get none at all —
media_split cannot draw an .inline-cta and gallery_marquee is preamble-only. Those last
two are recorded gaps, not omissions.
FOUR GAPS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A MARKUP SHAPE THE PAGE INVENTED RATHER THAN A FIELD
SOMEONE FORGOT. #issues has a page-local `.issues-grid` 5-up; #process hangs a
`.process-sub` <h3> mid-prose and an `.inline-cta.dark` under the grid; #options nests a
`<ul class="prep-list">` and a second paragraph inside its featured card and wraps all
three cards in stretched links; #results puts a two-button `.cta-row` inside a
gallery band's section-head. No field was added and no layout was invented for any of
them. See `known_gaps` on each block.

known_gaps: THE SECOND BUTTON LOSES ITS HOVER LABEL. Both buttons are carried by the two cta pairs
above, all four sub-fields on the deployed layout, and the first is exact.
MediaSplitBlock derives each hover label from the HREF rather than from a field
(CTA_HOVER, MediaSplitBlock.astro:233-238), and the map has four destinations:
#consult, #process, #faq and the practice phone number. `#options` is not among them,
so the second button comes back with no `data-hover` attribute and with "Treatment
Options" in its .l2 span, where the template ships data-hover="See Options" and
"See Options" (smile-makeover.astro:324, Button.astro:61-64). The visible resting label
is unchanged; what is lost is the word that slides up on hover.
The first button is exact: #consult -> "Get a Video", which is what :321 passes.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: one more entry in that CTA_HOVER map, `"#options": "See Options"`.
It is a component change and not a field — a hover label is chrome, not copy, and
giving an editor a field for it is how one page ends up with a hover word that
contradicts its button. This is the same residue teeth-whitening records for #process
-> "View Levels".

blocks.columns_evidence: .smilemakeover .issues-grid is repeat(5, 1fr) (smile-makeover.css:363-364) against five card rows. The card_grid `columns` select offers only 2, 3 and 4 (vs-content-model.php:1571-1583) and CardGridBlock emits a modifier only at 3 or 4 (CardGridBlock.astro:132), so 5 cannot be stored.
blocks.columns_is_wrong_on_purpose: "4", not "5" and not "2". "5" is not a choice the field has and the backfill would store a value ACF drops. "2" would emit no modifier at all and hand the row to the page sheet's `.smilemakeover .why-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr }` (smile-makeover.css:305) — five cards two across, which is further from the five-across the band has than four across is. So the band comes back four across with the fifth card wrapping, the same shape porcelain-veneers' five-step process band had before the process_steps select gained its fifth choice.

cards.from_cms: The five `cards` rows in group `issuesList`, in order — verified live: "Severe staining that no longer responds to whitening" through "Disproportionate tooth-to-gum ratio (gummy smile)". Title filled, body and meta null on all five. MOVED, not transcribed: the template's `issuesList` array (smile-makeover.astro:103-109) is a second copy of these same five lines and it is the else-branch copy, not the source.
cards.num_note: The `.num` divs read 01 through 05, derived by the template as String(i+1).padStart(2,'0') (smile-makeover.astro:351). They are not transcribed: `numbered` above makes CardGridBlock derive them from row position with the identical expression (CardGridBlock.astro:148), so a reorder cannot leave the numbering out of sequence.
cards.no_lead_no_body_note: Only `title` is mapped. The card rows have body and meta null and the template's card carries exactly one line of text, so `lead`, `body` and `body_2` are all left empty — CardGridBlock draws each of them only when non-empty.

known_gaps: THE PAGE-LOCAL 5-UP `.issues-grid` IS NOT REPRODUCED. THIS IS THE LARGEST LOSS ON THE
ROUTE AND ALL OF IT IS MARKUP — every word survives.
The template draws `<div class="issues-grid">` of five
`<article class="issues-card">`, each holding `<div class="num">` and
`<div class="label">` (smile-makeover.astro:347-356). CardGridBlock draws
`<div class="why-grid cols-4">` of five `<article class="why-card">`, each holding
`<div class="num">` and `<h3>` (CardGridBlock.astro:172-188). So three things change:
1. the grid is four across instead of five (see columns_is_wrong_on_purpose above);
2. the wrapper and card class names change, so the whole `.issues-*` rule set
(smile-makeover.css:363-388 — 30px italic sage-soft number, 15px 500-weight ink
label, 18px gap, sage-soft hover border) stops matching and the `.why-card` rules
(smile-makeover.css:306-330 — 42px padding, 36px number, 22px display h3) apply
instead;
3. each bullet becomes an `<h3>` rather than a `<div class="label">`, which is a
heading-level change on five sentences that are not headings.
NO FIELD WOULD CLOSE THIS AND NONE WAS ADDED. What closes it is one of two component
changes, in this order of preference:
a. a `5` choice on the card_grid Columns select (vs-content-model.php:1571-1583) plus
a `.why-grid.cols-5` rule in CardGridBlock.astro — the exact pair that closed
porcelain-veneers' five-column process band. That fixes (1) alone and leaves (2)
and (3);
b. folding `.issues-grid` into `.why-grid` in this page's stylesheet, so the five
cards keep their chrome under the class the block emits. That is an edit to the
else branch's own rules and has to wait until the else branch is retired.
Not attempted here, and deliberately: (b) repaints the un-migrated page, and this
phase's rollback path is that the un-migrated page still renders exactly as it does
today.
The five sentences, their order, their numbering and the band's id, rail entry,
eyebrow, heading and intro paragraph are all carried.

known_gaps: TWO ELEMENTS OF THIS BAND HAVE NO FIELD ON ANY REGISTERED LAYOUT. This is the lossiest
band on the page.
1. THE `.process-sub` SUB-HEADING. smile-makeover.astro:392 is

`

Preview Your New Smile Before You Commit

`, sitting
BETWEEN the two prose paragraphs. media_split's `.prose` is `body` then `body_2` and
nothing between them (MediaSplitBlock.astro:464-476). The words are lost and so is
the document structure — the second paragraph loses its heading.

IT IS NOT SMUGGLED THROUGH `body_2`. That field is rendered as `

` unless
the value opens with p/div/ul/ol/blockquote (MediaSplitBlock.astro:326-327), and
`<h3` is not in that list — so an h3 typed into it would be nested inside a
paragraph, which is invalid and which the parser's recovery turns into a stray empty

`the_rule_that_governs_every_value_below` forbids.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `body_heading_2` (or, better named, `prose_heading`) text
sub-field on media_split drawn between `body` and `body_2`, blank on every saved row
so it is additive — the same shape stat_callout's `body_heading` already has for the
<h3> that opens `.lasting-body`. One field, one component conditional, and it serves
any page that breaks a prose column with a sub-head.
2. THE `.inline-cta.dark` STRIP. smile-makeover.astro:414-425 is a full-width sage-deep
panel under the grid: `.ic-text` reading "Ready to see your preview? <em>Book online
and we'll take it from here." and `.ic-buttons` holding Book Online (light, to
the booking URL) and Call + the practice number (ghost-light). The whole panel is
lost, and with it the band's only conversion point.
The layout that HAS this field is process_steps — `cta_text`, drawn as the same
`.inline-cta` with the same two buttons (ProcessStepsBlock) — and this band is not a
process_steps band: it has no steps at all, and this page's `process_steps` repeater
is null. Choosing process_steps to keep the strip would draw a `.section-head` and an
empty `.process-grid` where the page has a `.natural-grid` with a photo in it, which
loses more than it saves.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `cta_text` sub-field on media_split, drawn by MediaSplitBlock
after the grid exactly as ProcessStepsBlock draws it — the two components already
agree on the markup, so this is moving one existing block of template, not designing
anything. Blank on both live media_split rows, so additive.
Everything else on the band is carried: eyebrow, heading, pull quote, both prose
paragraphs, the photo with its alt, the column order and the wider media column.

literal.title: Porcelain Veneers
literal.body: Porcelain veneers (thin custom shells bonded to the front of teeth) are Dr. Richardson's specialty and the most common centerpiece of a smile makeover plan. Vivid Smiles offers three prep levels:

literal.title: Invisalign and Orthodontic Alignment
literal.body: Correcting tooth position before placing veneers typically produces cleaner, longer-lasting results. Vivid Smiles offers Invisalign either as a preparatory step or as a standalone cosmetic solution for patients whose primary concern is alignment.

literal.title: Teeth Whitening
literal.body: Professional KOR whitening reaches shades not achievable with at-home products and can serve as a standalone solution or a prep step before veneers, delivering results that hold for years rather than weeks.

tiers.from_template: smile-makeover.astro:458-516 — the three .compare-card articles, the FIRST of them .featured with a .ribbon. The only `cards` rows on this page are the five in group `issuesList`, claimed by the `issues` block, so these three are transcribed rather than moved.
tiers.featured_is_first_here: The featured card is the FIRST of the three (smile-makeover.astro:458), like the pilot's and unlike porcelain-veneers' and teeth-whitening's, which are third. Position is carried by row order, so the flag travels with the first row and nothing else has to say so. It matters more on this page than on the others: `.compare-card.featured { grid-column: 1 / -1 }` makes the flagged card span the full row, so moving the flag moves the layout.
tiers.repeater_name_note: `tiers`, not `cards` and not `plans`. comparison_cards, card_grid and pricing_tiers do not share a repeater name — a repeater mints its GraphQL type from its field name, so sharing one merges two types and drops one side's sub-fields.
bullets_deliberately_unused: `tiers.bullets` EXISTS ON THE DEPLOYED LAYOUT AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT USED HERE, which
is why the prep-list is a gap below rather than a row in this list.
It is a block_list_field() repeater in the PHP and ComparisonCardsBlock does draw it
(ComparisonCardsBlock.astro:239-245). Two independent reasons not to reach for it:
comparison_cards fragment is `tiers { tag title body ribbon featured }`. A value
written to a field the query does not select is a value that never arrives;
2. even selected, the component draws `<ul>` of plain-text `<li>` — no `prep-list`
class and no <strong> label inside each line. This page styles only
would arrive unstyled and with its three bold labels flattened into the
Writing it anyway would move the words into markup this sheet does not paint, which is

blocks.cta_note: ComparisonCardsBlock draws the closing .cta-row itself — Free Virtual Consult to #consult (sage, "Get a Video"), Read FAQ to #faq (ghost, "See Answers"), and the note "No commitment · Personal video reply" (ComparisonCardsBlock.astro:265-279). That is exactly what smile-makeover.astro:519-527 ships, variants included, because this is a paper band and isDarkBand is false. The layout has no cta sub-fields, so this map supplies nothing.
blocks.no_callout_note: No `callout_heading` / `callout_body`: this band has no aside. The .safety-callout that fills those on teeth-whitening has no counterpart here, and supplying them would add an <aside> this page has never had.
known_gaps: THREE THINGS ON THIS BAND HAVE NO FIELD, AND TWO OF THEM ARE ON THE FEATURED CARD.
1. THE `<ul class="prep-list">` NESTED INSIDE THE FEATURED CARD.
smile-makeover.astro:471-483 is a three-line list inside .compare-card.featured, each
line a <strong> label followed by a description:
Traditional veneers: Minimal enamel removal; considered permanent; 20+ year lifespan
Minimal-prep veneers: Less enamel reduction while preserving more natural tooth structure
No-prep veneers: No enamel removal; reversible when candidacy allows
A LIST NESTED IN A CARD IS THE SHAPE comparison_cards HAS NO QUERYABLE SUB-FIELD FOR.
`tiers.bullets` is the nearest thing and is unusable for the two reasons in
`bullets_deliberately_unused` above. The three lines are lost, and the paragraph
above them ("…offers three prep levels:") comes back ending in a colon that
introduces nothing.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: add `bullets { lead item }` to the comparison_cards fragment in
manifest.ts AND teach ComparisonCardsBlock to draw it as `<ul class="prep-list">`
with the `lead` half in <b>, which is the treatment MediaSplitBlock already gives
`checklist` (MediaSplitBlock.astro:451-459). Both halves in one commit — selecting
the field without the markup change would produce an unstyled list, which reads as
supported and is not.
2. THE FEATURED CARD'S SECOND PARAGRAPH. smile-makeover.astro:484-488:
"Color, shape, and translucency are customized to your facial features, skin tone, and preferences. The goal is results that enhance your existing smile, not overwrite it."
A `tiers` row has one `body`. The card ships two paragraphs with a list between them,
so the second is lost whole.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `body_2` textarea on `tiers`, drawn as a second

after the
bullets — the same field, the same name and the same blank-is-additive rule that
card_grid's and media_split's `body_2` already carry. Note the ORDER: on this card
the second paragraph comes AFTER the list, so the component must draw body, bullets,
body_2 in that sequence.
3. THE THREE STRETCHED LINKS. Each card opens with
`<a class="compare-card__stretch" href=… aria-label=…>` covering the whole card
(smile-makeover.astro:459-462, 491-494, 505-508) — to porcelain-veneers,
clear-aligners and teeth-whitening respectively. comparison_cards has no href on a
tier, so all three cards come back unclickable, `.compare-card { cursor: pointer }`
(smile-makeover.css:411) becomes a lie, and three internal links leave the page.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: `href` and `link_label` text sub-fields on `tiers`, with
ComparisonCardsBlock emitting the anchor only when href is filled. card_grid already
declares an unused `cards[].href` for the same reason, so the field shape is settled;
what is not settled is the aria-label, which is per-card copy and needs its own
sub-field rather than being derived from the title.
Carried in full: all three tags, all three titles, the ribbon, the featured flag and
with it the full-width span, the first paragraph of every card, the section-head from
the CMS row, and the closing cta-row the component owns.

literal.title: Dr. Bryce Richardson's Cosmetic Dentistry Expertise
literal.body: Dr. Richardson earned his DDS from Indiana University School of Dentistry, graduated at the top of his class clinically, and has completed 600+ hours of specialized esthetic and surgical training. He served on staff at Implant Pathway, one of the country's most respected implant training facilities, and is a Parker resident and active community member. His approach is consistent across every case: enhance your natural features rather than replace them, working toward Vivid Smiles' goal of becoming Colorado's leading cosmetic dental destination.

literal.title: Advanced Technology for Predictable Results
literal.body: Digital scanning eliminates traditional impressions, and in-house milling units and 3D printers reduce wait time on custom restorations. CBCT 3D imaging provides a complete diagnostic picture before treatment begins, and digital smile design connects the full technology stack to a preview you can see and refine. Every tool at Vivid Smiles is selected for what it does for the patient: less time waiting, more confidence in the outcome.

caption.literal: Custom timeline based on your plan

intro_2.literal: For investment, cost reflects the scope of your plan. Vivid Smiles provides transparent pricing and discusses financing options at the consultation, so there are no surprises after you commit. Patients who are uninsured or looking for additional cost flexibility may benefit from the practice's in-house dental membership plan. Most cosmetic procedures are considered elective and are not covered by dental insurance, though treatments that address both cosmetic and functional concerns may qualify for partial coverage.

That is exactly the shape GalleryMarqueeBlock draws — `.section` > `.wrap` >

blocks.reveal_note: This band's <section> carries no data-vs-reveal-batch, with data-vs-reveal on the .section-head instead (smile-makeover.astro:624, 626). GalleryMarqueeBlock emits exactly that pair (GalleryMarqueeBlock.astro:151, 153), so the attributes match without anything here saying so. blocks.tiles_note: No sub-fields beyond the preamble by design: the tiles are files read by src/lib/smiles.ts and doubled into a marquee track by the component, the same source and the same doubling the template does at :648-660. Nothing to move.

known_gaps: TWO, ONE OF THEM COSTING TWO BUTTONS AND TWO INTERNAL LINKS.
1. THE `.cta-row` INSIDE THE SECTION-HEAD. smile-makeover.astro:630-641 puts a cta-row
INSIDE `.section-head`, holding View the Smile Gallery (light, /smile-gallery/,
hover "Open Gallery") and Patient Stories (ghost-light, /patient-testimonials/, hover
"Read Stories"). gallery_marquee is preamble-only — `anchor navLabel band eyebrow
heading body` and nothing else (manifest.ts:265-268) — so both buttons are lost, and
with them the page's only links to the gallery and testimonial pages.
THIS IS THE ONE GAP ON THE ROUTE THAT COSTS NAVIGATION RATHER THAN CHROME. The two
destinations appear nowhere else on the page: the breadcrumb goes up to
/cosmetic-dentistry/, the #options cards link to the three sibling service pages, and
the closing VirtualConsult and FinalBand link to neither.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: `cta_label` / `cta_href` and `cta_label_2` / `cta_href_2` on
gallery_marquee, drawn inside `.section-head` after the body paragraph — the field
set media_split already carries, in the position this template puts it. The hover
labels are the same derived-from-href problem the `what` band records: neither
/smile-gallery/ nor /patient-testimonials/ is in any CTA_HOVER map today, so closing
this properly means adding both destinations there as well.
NOT closed by moving this band to another layout. faq, card_grid and media_split all
have cta fields and all three draw a `.cta-row` OUTSIDE the section-head, add a
data-vs-reveal-batch this band does not have, and none of them draws the marquee at
all.
2. THE EYEBROW GAINS A `light` CLASS. GalleryMarqueeBlock hard-codes
`<span class="eyebrow light">` (GalleryMarqueeBlock.astro:154) rather than deriving
it from the band the way every other block does, and this template ships a plain
`<span class="eyebrow">` at :627. Visually inert on this page —
`.smilemakeover .section.alt .eyebrow` (0,3,0) at smile-makeover.css:263 beats
`.eyebrow.light` — but it is a byte in the HTML and scripts/vr-html.mjs compares
bytes.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: give GalleryMarqueeBlock the same `eyebrowLight` derivation the
other five band blocks share (band === sage || sage-pale). That is safe for the two
migrated siblings, whose gallery bands are sage-pale and sage and therefore keep the
class they have today.
Carried: the eyebrow text, the heading, the intro paragraph, the id, the rail entry, the
reveal attributes and the marquee itself.
